title: Container/Kubernetes Escape
description: Privileged containers, sockets, capabilities, and Kubernetes tokens
detail:
Determine whether you are in a container: /.dockerenv exists, cgroup contains docker/kubepods.
1. Privileged: use fdisk -l to find the host disk; mount it to /mnt → chroot and write a cron job/SSH key
2. /var/run/docker.sock is mounted: start a privileged container that mounts the host
3. Capabilities: CAP_SYS_ADMIN can mount the cgroup release_agent; CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH can read arbitrary files
4. Kubernetes: the ServiceAccount token is at /var/run/secrets/.../token → use the API server to create a privileged pod
5. Kernel vulnerabilities also apply (the host kernel is shared)
After escaping, first look for sensitive target files on the host and collect cloud credentials (metadata/configuration files).
